components.title: AI-native architectures and testing challenges
components.teaches: Students will identify the distinctive characteristics of AI-native software (data‑driven behavior, non‑determinism, model drift) and explain why traditional testing approaches fall short. They will list at least three testing challenges unique to AI components.

components.title: Unit testing mechanisms for ML models
components.teaches: Students will describe property‑based testing, metamorphic testing, and model‑behavior contracts as unit‑level mechanisms for ML models. They will apply one mechanism to a sample classifier and articulate the trade‑off between coverage and oracle cost.

components.title: Integration testing for AI pipelines
components.teaches: Students will explain contract testing, data‑drift detection, and end‑to‑end pipeline validation as integration mechanisms. They will compare how each mechanism handles versioned models and evolving data schemas.

components.title: Model quality evaluation metrics
components.teaches: Students will define accuracy, fairness, robustness, and calibration metrics and explain when each is appropriate for AI-native systems. They will compute a fairness disparity metric on a provided confusion matrix.

components.title: System-level evaluation metrics
components.teaches: Students will describe latency, throughput, cost, and reliability metrics for deployed AI services. They will analyse a scenario to decide which system‑level metric dominates the testing budget.

components.title: Comparative framework for testing selection
components.teaches: Students will use a decision matrix (mechanism vs. metric vs. risk) to compare and select appropriate testing mechanisms and evaluation metrics for a given AI-native architecture. They will justify their choices with respect to risk tolerance and resource constraints.

video.description:
Learn how to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) using an enterprise-grade evaluation framework designed for AI applications in production. This tutorial covers the essential metrics, testing strategies, and monitoring techniques used by AI architects to measure model quality, reliability, safety, and business performance.

You'll explore how to evaluate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems by measuring both retrieval quality and answer generation accuracy. The video also explains advanced validation techniques such as Chain of Verification (CoVe), AI benchmarking, agent evaluation, hallucination detection, and human-in-the-loop review for building trustworthy AI applications.

This video introduces a new series on testing AI agents, focusing on why traditional evaluation methods fall short for autonomous systems. Discover what "agent evaluation" truly means, encompassing the entire AI stack from the LLM brain to external tools and memory. We explore a full stack checklist for system level testing and highlight the unique challenges of multi-agent evaluation, providing a real life example to illustrate these concepts.
